newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Prompt demand props up gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Prompt demand props up gas oil.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps opened steady at midday on Monday in quiet trading as the market looked to local demand and firmer crude for support, traders said.
"The market is looking to local buying interest for support as demand from China slows down ahead of the Chinese New Year holidays," one trader said.
Front-month January gas oil swaps were last quoted at $30.20/$30.40 per barrel, from Friday's $31.15/$31.35, brokers said.
February was last quoted at $30.10/$30.30, against Friday's $29.90/$30.00.
A local trader had throughout last week bought a total of five 150,000-barrel cargoes at between $32.30-$30.65 a barrel free-on-board Singapore.
Brokers said the firmer prices were also due to stronger crude values on the after hours ACCESS market where February WTI was up 32 cents to $26.41 a barrel at 0400 GMT.

Traders said the fundamentals remain bearish as demand from China, especially for February cargoes, have slowed down considerably as the market winds down for the Lunar New year which begins on February 7.
Usually the Chinese market is closed for about 10-days for the holidays, they said.
Sentiment was also dampened by India's decision to buy only 135,000-tonnes in its February supplementary tender against an initial market expectation of 200,000-tonnes.
Traders said the upcoming sale tender from Taiwan where up to three 225,000-250,000 barrels cargoes maybe sold is another bearish factor.
Fuel oil is still under selling pressure as the market was weighed down by ample supplies and poor Chinese demand.
Front-month January was last quoted at $115.75/$116.75 per tonne, from Friday's $116.25/$117.00, brokers said.
On Friday, in the physical market, a major offered 20,000-tonne loading in February 3-7 at $118.00 per tonne, down $3 a tonne from Thursday's offer price.
